caption: The clothes and lots are one of the closest Gospel links to Psalm 22. It is clear literary fulfilment—but not independent proof of an advance forecast.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 22 predict the divided clothes? The psalm says enemies divide the sufferer’s clothes by lot. Luke describes people doing exactly that to Jesus.
slides.body: The psalm says enemies divide the sufferer’s clothes by lot. Luke describes people doing exactly that to Jesus.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 22 predict the divided clothes?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 22:17-18: They divide my garments … and cast lots for my clothing.
slides.body: They divide my garments … and cast lots for my clothing.
slides.heading: Ps 22:17-18

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Lk 23:34–35, BSB: They divided up His garments by casting lots. The people stood watching, and the rulers sneered at Him.
slides.body: They divided up His garments by casting lots. The people stood watching, and the rulers sneered at Him.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Lk 23:34–35

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: This is a very close match The clothes, the lots and the watching crowd appear together. John even calls the action fulfilled Scripture.
slides.body: The clothes, the lots and the watching crowd appear together. John even calls the action fulfilled Scripture.
slides.heading: This is a very close match

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The link is real—but what proves what? The Gospels use Psalm 22 to explain Jesus’s death. That does not prove the psalm began as a forecast of him.
slides.body: The Gospels use Psalm 22 to explain Jesus’s death. That does not prove the psalm began as a forecast of him.
slides.heading: The link is real—but what proves what?

title: Clothes divided by lot
